judgements.reason: PDF pp. 1–9 contain the title page, seven numbered body pages and the Code and Data / Author Contributions block before the References, so non-reference, non-appendix content is nine physical pages against an eight-page cap.
The title page (PDF p. 1) prints 'Alejandro Castellanos' with an empty affiliation cell and a bare 'With / Apart Research' line whose role is undefined.

The report self-dates a 2026-11-09 correction (Code and Data, PDF p. 9; LLM Usage Statement, PDF p. 15) but gives no submission timestamp or timezone, so eligibility cannot be checked from the manuscript alone.

The 'judgement' delegated to auditors in §3.1–3.4 is inspection of receipt fields (build-only, wrong-artifact, wrong-run), which the kernel's binding/integrity checks are already structured to verify, and no worked release shows the receipt-to-claim vs attestation-to-binding split.
Contribution 5 (PDF p. 2) claims 'complete logs' while Appendix D (PDF p. 15) lists missing prompts, raw responses, executable revision, temperature and most retry fields.

§3.4 (PDF p. 5) asserts caps are kept non-binding by retries, but Appendix C.3 (PDF pp. 13–14) says retained records omit attempt arrays and B.3 shows the replacement run moved a 4-of-7 hidden capture from 1 to 0.

'do not scale' (Abstract, PDF p. 1), 'regardless of swarm size or model' (§1, PDF p. 2), 'every reachable state' (§3.2, PDF p. 4) and 'The guarantee also assumes' (Discussion, PDF p. 8) all outrun the stated bounded/conditional framing.
S2 (§3.2, PDF p. 4) checks immediate success of an eligible execution attempt, which is availability/execution correctness rather than temporal liveness under a fairness assumption.

Finding 2 (PDF p. 6) says 4-of-7 'matched the gated majority's safety at 10% collusion' on the strength of 0/24 observations versus 0/120, which is stronger than zero observed captures in twelve draws.
Table 1's caption (PDF p. 6) says shares 10–50%, but 96 = 8×12 and 48 = 4×12 include the 0% share runs while only the 120-target denominator excludes 0%.
Figure 1 (PDF p. 7) shows only 1-of-1, 2-of-3 and 4-of-7 although Table 1 records 23 and 20 captures for 3-of-5, contradicting its own caption ('regimes that were ever captured').
The bibliography (PDF pp. 9–10) uses the title fragment 'From Logic Monopoly (2026)' as author, a year-less SQLite entry, and mixed 'et al.' versus full author lists.
Table 1 splits the sentence resumed as 'targets give 120 target trials per regime' (PDF pp. 5–6) and Figure 1 splits Finding 3 across PDF p. 7.
MCP, A2A (§1), HMAC (§3.1) and TF-IDF (§3.4) appear without expansion and receipt/evidence/release/attestation are never defined by one concrete example.

'implements nothing, measures nothing' and 'two things no constitution allows' (PDF p. 2), 'the checker has teeth' (contribution 2) and 'unanimity buys safety with liveness' (Finding 3, PDF p. 6) are rhetorical rather than neutral.

The 12 targets and the near-miss cases (§3.4, §4.3) are exact field mismatches on structured receipts, so honest error is 0/746 and G3's correlated-error regime is never exercised (Abstract; §3.3, PDF p. 4).
Figure 1 plots only the a-priori G3 curve, and the 30→40% dip visible in Table 3 (PDF p. 13) is exactly the kind of 12-draw seed noise the paper's own Table 1 note (PDF p. 6) warns about.
§3.4 (PDF p. 5) never states how 1-of-1, 2-of-3 and 3-of-5 are sliced from the seven seated auditors, and Table 1 pools the visible-board half where auditors see the final tally before attesting.
Same as A.11: 3-of-5 is captured 23/20 times in Table 1 but missing from Figure 1 and Table 3 despite the caption's exhaustive wording.
The source confirms '\bibitem[SQLite()]{sqlite}' with empty year and a title-as-author entry for arXiv:2603.25100, plus literal 'et al.' in some entries.
The first author's affiliation field is empty on PDF p. 1 while the second lists University of Toronto.
B.2 and C.2 (PDF pp. 12–13) reduce to the fragments 'Table 2.' and 'Table 4.', and §5 uses \subsection* while Appendices B–C use run-in \head{}.

The audit and review-round disclosure is confined to Code and Data (PDF p. 9) and the LLM Usage Statement (PDF p. 15), which are back matter rather than the scientific narrative, and such disclosure is appropriate under the hackathon's AI-tools policy.

0/746 honest unsafe attestations (§4.3, PDF p. 7) leave G3's independence assumption untested, and the capture curves in Figure 1 are easy to over-transfer to judgement tasks despite the paper's caveats.

Finding 1 (PDF p. 6) concedes the forgery result is 'architectural by construction' (voters cannot verify an HMAC) and §3.4 plus Appendix D confirm the gated majority is executed with fresh synthetic keys.
The Table 1 note (PDF p. 6) itself states each regime has 60 not 120 independent draws and per-share cells are n = 12, so pooled counts invite over-reading without draw-level ranges.
The title page (PDF p. 1) leaves the first author's affiliation blank.
The 2026 arXiv entries and the SQLite/'From Logic Monopoly' items (PDF pp. 9–10) need verification and consistent author formatting, without any presumption of fabrication.
Figure 1's panels are narrow with the legend below the axes and Table 1's dagger footnote carries the paired-design information in footnotesize text (PDF pp. 6–7).
§4.3 (PDF p. 7) reports only an F1 range of 0.97–1.0 with one spurious cluster and no per-share precision/recall breakdown; the detector spec sits in B.4 (PDF p. 13).
Appendix D (PDF p. 15) documents the missing revision/temperature/request-ID/prompt fields, but §3.4 (PDF p. 5) presents the runs as if reproducibly specified.

revised_own_concerns.location: Title page (PDF p. 1); PDF pp. 2–8; Code and Data / Author Contributions (PDF p. 9)
revised_own_concerns.issue: Counting the title page, non-reference, non-appendix content spans nine physical pages (title page + seven numbered pages + the Code and Data and Author Contributions block before the References on PDF p. 9), against the hard eight-page cap.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Move 'Code and Data' and 'Author Contributions' into an appendix, and either merge the title/abstract into page 1 or obtain explicit organizer confirmation that the title page is exempt.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Alejandro Castellanos has no printed affiliation and 'With / Apart Research' does not state Apart's role.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add the affiliation (or 'Independent researcher') and label Apart Research explicitly as organizer, sponsor or affiliation.

revised_own_concerns.location: PDF pp. 9–10; in-text citations PDF pp. 2–3
revised_own_concerns.issue: Title-as-author 'From Logic Monopoly (2026)', year-less SQLite, mixed 'et al.' and full lists, and several 2026 arXiv IDs that should be checked to resolve.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Normalise to one author-year style, add SQLite's year/access date, and verify every arXiv ID and title against the source before publication.

revised_own_concerns.location: §3.4 (PDF p. 5); Finding 1 (PDF p. 6); Appendix D (PDF p. 15)
revised_own_concerns.issue: The decisive comparator for 'a committee adds no safety' is an offline reconstruction executed with fresh synthetic receipts and keys, so it cannot re-authenticate the original receipts.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: State the equivalence argument once in §3.4, and add a one-line sanity check that the reconstructed kernel rejects a tampered receipt identically to the live path.

revised_own_concerns.issue: 'Non-reasoning models were excluded so that reasoning mode would not be confounded with family' is a sampling choice, not a deconfound of reasoning.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Rewrite as: 'Both models use reasoning mode, so reasoning is held constant; this design cannot separate reasoning effects from family effects and says nothing about non-reasoning models.'

revised_own_concerns.location: Table 1 (PDF p. 6); Figure 1 (PDF p. 7); Table 3 (PDF p. 13)
revised_own_concerns.issue: Pooled 120-target counts come from 60 independent draws with n=12 per share cell, no intervals or realized G2 seat-bound markers are shown, and the 30→40% dip in Figure 1 is unreadable as behavioural signal.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add realized G2 seat-opportunity markers or counts per share to Figure 1/Table 3, and one caption sentence stating that per-share binomial intervals would be on the order of ±20 percentage points.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Appendix subheads are run-in bolded paragraphs while §5 uses \subsection*, B.2 and C.2 reduce to 'Table 2.' and 'Table 4.', and Table 2 omits step counts for three mutants.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Use one subsection style throughout, expand the two fragments into sentences, and fill or mark 'n/a' the missing counterexample lengths in Table 2.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The references end near the top of PDF p. 10, leaving an almost empty page before the appendices.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Let Appendix A begin on that page or tighten the bibliography so the references end on PDF p. 9.

revised_own_concerns.issue: One paragraph mixes 0/746 seats, 108 case-conditions, 508 honest seats and 8/492 refusals, and Table 4 uses n=756 seats, so units must be reconciled to follow the key negative result.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add one unit gloss at first use in §4.3: 'seats = auditor slots; case-conditions = runs × cases; committees = capture events'.

new_concerns.location: Table 1 (PDF p. 6), caption vs column denominators
new_concerns.issue: The caption says outcomes are pooled over colluder shares 10–50%, but 'Valid released (of 96)' and 'Forged released (of 48)' correspond to 8×12 and 4×12, which include the 0% share runs, while only the 120-target denominator excludes 0%.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: State the sampling range per column group, or recompute all columns over the same nonzero shares and note why 0% targets are excluded.

new_concerns.issue: The caption says it plots 'the committee regimes that were ever captured', but Committee 3-of-5 (23/20 captures in Table 1) is omitted from both the figure and Table 3.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Revise the caption to 'selected committee regimes' or add a 3-of-5 panel and a Table 3 column.

new_concerns.location: Contribution 5 (PDF p. 2) vs Appendix D (PDF p. 15)
new_concerns.issue: 'An open harness with complete logs' is contradicted by Appendix D, which lists missing prompts, raw responses, executable revision, temperature, provider request IDs and most retry metadata.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Replace 'complete logs' with an accurate description of retained logical records, and state the reproducibility boundary in §3.4.

new_concerns.issue: S2 ('an eligible execution attempt succeeds') is immediate execution correctness, not temporal liveness, so the abstract's claim that exploration 'confirms its safety, liveness … invariants' uses the term too strongly.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Rename S2 to 'eligible-execution success' and adjust the abstract wording, or state explicitly the restricted meaning of 'liveness'.

new_concerns.location: §3.4 (PDF p. 5); Appendix B.3 and C.3 (PDF pp. 12–14)
new_concerns.issue: The main-text claim that caps were kept non-binding by retries cannot be verified for most historical records (missing attempt arrays), and the one documented re-run changed a 4-of-7 hidden capture from 1 to 0, yet no main-text sensitivity statement appears.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Qualify the §3.4 claim to match the retained evidence and add a one-sentence sensitivity note (original vs re-run, 13/14 cells identical, one cell 1→0) in the main text.

new_concerns.location: Code and Data (PDF p. 9); LLM Usage Statement (PDF p. 15)
new_concerns.issue: A 2026-11-09 audit/correction is described without timestamps or timezones, so eligibility under the Nov 8 AoE deadline and the boundary between sprint work and later corrections cannot be assessed.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide the submitted commit/PDF hash with timezone and state which analyses and controls were completed before the deadline, including when the gated-majority control was added.

new_concerns.issue: The paper never states how 1-of-1, 2-of-3 and 3-of-5 committees are sliced from the seven-seat draw, and Table 1 pools visible-board runs (where auditors see the 50-agent tally before attesting) into the 'standalone committee' comparison.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: State the slicing rule explicitly and report capture counts split by visible vs hidden board so readers can verify the standalone-committee claim.

new_concerns.location: Abstract (PDF p. 1); §1 Theory of change (PDF p. 2); §3.2 (PDF p. 4); Discussion (PDF p. 8)
new_concerns.issue: Global statements ('do not scale', 'regardless of swarm size or model', 'every reachable state', 'The guarantee also assumes') blur the careful G1–G3 separation and the depth/action bounds.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Say 'all states reachable within the stated world, action set and depth bound', frame gateway scaling as an architectural proposition, and name G1, G2 or G3 whenever assumptions are discussed.

rebuttals.response: Agreed, and note the cheap fix: the numbered body is only seven pages (PDF pp. 2–8), so moving Code and Data / Author Contributions (PDF p. 9) into an appendix plus a note on whether the title page counts resolves the cap.

The manuscript frames 2026-11-09 as a presentation/statistics/provenance correction with no new model observations (PDF p. 9), but I agree timestamps with timezones and the pre/post-deadline split are needed to settle eligibility rather than inferred from a calendar date.

I disagree that this damages the narrative: the correction and review-round disclosure sits only in back matter (PDF pp. 9, 15) and the hackathon explicitly permits AI tools, though the 'three weak rejects and one reject' detail could be trimmed as superfluous.
Agreed on verification, with the caveat you draw: entries such as arXiv:2605.20704 or 2608.15888 must be checked against the source and absence of a resolvable record must not be read as fabrication.

The slicing rule is genuinely absent from §3.4 (PDF p. 5), and the visible/hidden pooling matters because the text itself says only hidden-board committees 'do not depend on the vote', so this should be fixed in the methods, not only in an appendix.
